Earlier this year, there were rumors that iOS 26.4 would launch a revamped Health app. The plan was subsequently postponed, and after the release of iOS 27, this overhaul has still not materialized.

With the next-generation Apple Watch Series 12 and Ultra 4 set to debut next month, it's worth asking: will these new features be unveiled alongside the new hardware?

Precedent

First, it's necessary to explain why these features are most likely to launch in September. You might think: "Shouldn't all software be announced in June?" But in fact, there is indeed precedent for similar situations.

The Low Power Mode in watchOS 9, the sleep apnea detection feature in watchOS 11, and the hypertension notifications in watchOS 26 were all announced in September, even though they don't functionally depend on the latest hardware.

Based on these reasons, even though the latest Health app upgrade may not require a brand-new Apple Watch, Apple is still highly likely to choose to wait until September for the official announcement.

There's still time

Before WWDC27, Bloomberg reporter Mark Gurman had already warned that the new Health app upgrade (codenamed Project Mulberry) might not appear in the WWDC keynote. This prediction ultimately proved accurate:

Does this mean Project Mulberry is guaranteed to appear at the September event? Not necessarily. However, given the precedent of new features being announced in September on multiple occasions, and given that we've known for a while it could arrive a bit later than WWDC, the chances of a September debut are still quite high—even if it might ultimately have to wait until October, arriving alongside iOS 27.1.

Feature recap

The rumors about these features have been constantly changing, because there are simply too many variables involved. You may have heard that one of the ideas was to launch a standalone Health+ service with videos narrated by doctors. However, according to reports, those plans have been scaled back, and the features will ultimately be integrated into the existing Health app experience.

That said, two features are fairly clear: first, an AI health coach will be added, providing suggestions based on your Health app data; second, the camera will be used to offer real-time guidance for fitness and other health-related activities. Another key part of this upgrade is a completely new design for the Health app, making it easier for you to understand all the data.

Beyond this, we can only wait and see. Personally, I'm really looking forward to a much better way to organize and understand my Apple health data.
